subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as part of the core bootstrap-extra-files hook contract?
rationale: The choice changes deterministic system-prompt context and user-facing hook configuration semantics, so it needs maintainer product/security-boundary intent rather than an autonomous bug-fix decision.

options.title: Approve explicit in-workspace files
options.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, session filtering, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary file injection and keep operators on first-class workspace filenames or manual reads.

options.title: Defer to broader context API
options.body: Leave this issue open until a larger maintainer-approved context-loading contract covers discovery, trust, and session scoping.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit in-workspace files
recommendation.body: Allow custom basenames only when explicitly configured and still protected by workspace containment, size budgets, session filtering, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original bootstrap-extra-files work and has direct boundary-read history in the relevant loader path.
